approach: Add `check_request_coverage(reading, request)` in a new module `crates/athena-core/src/reading/coverage.rs` (declared in reading.rs with `mod coverage;` and `pub use coverage::*;`). It parses the request's acceptance bullets and refuses, naming each missing bullet verbatim, when the reading's criteria do not cover one. Parsing: find the first line that is a bare `Acceptance:` heading (case-insensitive, optional markdown `#`/`*`, optional `criteria`); collect the lines after it for which the existing `is_bullet` (`-`, `*`, `N.`; topics.rs:266) is true; stop at the first blank line once a bullet was seen, or at a `Files:` line; a non-bullet line in between is a wrapped continuation and is skipped. A request with no such heading, or with no bullets under it, asks for nothing. Coverage is measured over the union of all criteria, because a reading may legitimately split one bullet over several criteria (this job's own reading splits the 'fmt, clippy ... CHANGELOG.md' bullet over criteria 5 and 7). A bullet is covered when (a) it has distinctive tokens (a piece containing `/`, an interior `.`, or starting `--`, trimmed of quotes, backticks and punctuation, lowercased) and every one appears in the lowercased criteria text, or (b) at least half, rounded up, of its distinct stems appear among the stems of all criteria. Stems come from the existing `request_words` (outcome.rs:141, lowercase, keeps `a.b`), minus a short stop list, minus words of two letters or fewer, with a trailing `ing`, `ed`, `es` or `s` stripped when four or more letters remain; no stem or stop-list helper exists in the crate (searched `fn stem`, `STOP`), so the module defines its own small ones. The check does nothing (Ok) for a reading that declines (`capability` is None) or asks a question (`question` is Some): a split may be proposed only as that question, never by dropping a bullet. It also does nothing when the request allows a split: the non-bullet lines of the request, lowercased, hold one of the phrases `may split`, `can split`, `could split`, `split it`, `split this`, `split the job`, `split into`, `be split`, `in parts`, `in separate jobs`, `separate jobs`, `one part at a time`, not preceded within 12 characters by `not `, `never ` or `n't `. This job's own request ('rejected for a split the reading itself chose', 'allows a split', 'propose a split only as a question') holds none of those phrases, so it is still checked. Wiring: one `step!(check_request_coverage(reading, request));` line, placed LAST in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references`. The brief's reading said after `check_outcome_state`, but three existing tests assert that step's neighbours (reading.rs:4911 governance then outcome, :5394 outcome then environment_reach, :7417 environment_reach then defined_terms), so that spot would break them; last also leaves the first-refusing check of every existing refusing corpus case unchanged. The doc of `check_reading_acceptance` gains a `[`check_request_coverage`]` link in its ordered list. The new check's doc names the 2026-10-29 job that was rejected for a split the reading chose (the request of job 20261029-111121-fzx0 describes it; its own id is not recorded in any file the planner can read), says a split may be proposed only as a question, never by dropping a bullet, and states 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' with 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' marked as an estimate. Tests in reading.rs use `governed_reading` (reading.rs:4527, content criteria, passes all earlier checks with `repo_files` None) and real request strings. Corpus: a `coverage_cases()` group is added to `cases()` in refusal_corpus.rs, 7 new input-form tags are added to `INPUT_FORMS` (52 to 59), `reading_source()` in both reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs gains `include_str!` of coverage.rs (otherwise the doc/step/mechanism tests cannot find the new function), and CHANGELOG.md gets an Unreleased/Added entry.

decisions.choice: Place the step last in refusing_check, after check_reading_references.
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert the neighbours of check_outcome_state, check_environment_reach and check_code_survey (reading.rs:4911, 5394, 7417, 8116), so inserting after check_outcome_state breaks them. Last also means no existing refusing case changes its first refusing check; only accept cases with an `Acceptance:` heading can be newly refused. The refusal still happens at reading acceptance, before any producer run, which is what the request asks for.

rejected.option: Insert directly after check_outcome_state as the reading assumed
rejected.why: Breaks the adjacency assertions at reading.rs:5394 (outcome_state then environment_reach) and would need those tests rewritten for no gain.

rejected.option: Call the check directly inside check_reading_acceptance
rejected.why: refusing_check's doc and the corpus test that scans check_reading_acceptance for a direct `check_` call (refusal_corpus.rs ~2969) require a step! line, and the corpus needs the name to prove a refusing case.

decisions.choice: Read bullets only under an `Acceptance:` heading, ending at a blank line or a `Files:` line; a request without the heading is not checked.
decisions.reason: That is the shape of the failing request, and of every steward-, Hestia- and user-made request (steward.rs:581). Bullets elsewhere in a request (background lists, quoted text) are not acceptance. Scoping to the heading also keeps the many scripted-reader tests in other crates, whose requests have bullets but no heading (grep of `Acceptance:` over crates/ found only steward.rs, hestia.rs, code_health.rs, reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs), outside the new rule. A corpus case pins the no-heading gap as known.

rejected.why: Treats any list in the request as acceptance and would newly refuse readings in tests and records whose requests carry bullets that are not acceptance; the brief's reading names the heading.

decisions.choice: Measure coverage over the union of all criteria, with the token-or-half-the-stems rule, and accept when unsure.
decisions.reason: A reading may split one bullet over several criteria (this job's reading does). A false refusal costs a reader run; the target is the wholesale drop of a bullet. The limits (a paraphrase that shares few words is refused; a bullet whose words are all common in other criteria passes) are stated in the doc.

rejected.option: Require one criterion to contain all of a bullet's words
rejected.why: Refuses readings that legitimately split a bullet over two criteria, such as this job's own reading.

rejected.option: Ask a model whether each bullet is covered
rejected.why: Reading checks are deterministic and call no model (checks.rs:219 doc); the check also runs in replay and check-reading with no agent.

decisions.choice: The request allows a split only through an affirmative phrase in its non-bullet lines, with a negation guard; the reading's own question exempts the reading.
decisions.reason: The failing request itself uses the words `split` and `follow-up` while forbidding the drop, so a bare keyword test would switch the check off for exactly the request it must protect. The question field is the only channel the brief allows for proposing a split.

rejected.why: Matches this job's own request text and the corpus request 'Follow up on job ...' (refusal_corpus.rs:1767), disabling the check where it matters.

rejected.option: Let the reading itself declare a split in an assumption or out_of_scope
rejected.why: That is the mechanism that caused the misread: the reading chose the split.

decisions.choice: Name every omitted bullet in one refusal, with the marker stripped and the text verbatim in quotes, on one line, starting 'the reading was refused because'.
decisions.reason: Matches the other checks' shape (no newline, starts with 'the reading was refused because', as asserted at reading.rs:4702-4706) and `check_reading_text` collapses white space, so verbatim text survives.

rejected.option: Name only the first omitted bullet
rejected.why: The reader has one correction round; naming all avoids a second refusal.

risks.risk: Existing tests or fixtures with an `Acceptance:` heading and a reading whose criteria do not repeat the bullets are newly refused (hestia.rs, steward.rs, code_health.rs and cli tests with a scripted reader). The planner could not run the suite.
risks.mitigation: The check is scoped to the heading, and identical text always counts as covered, so every `base_reading`/`stored_reading` fixture seen passes. Step 6 has the producer run `cargo test --locked` and, for any test the new check refuses, change that fixture's criteria to repeat the bullet text (never relax the check). The files in which a heading appears are known: steward.rs, hestia.rs, code_health.rs, reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs.

risks.risk: False refusals: a reading that paraphrases a bullet with few shared words (or gives only a file name where the bullet gives the crate-relative path) is refused although it covers it.
risks.mitigation: The rule accepts on either all distinctive tokens or half the stems over the union of all criteria, and exempts questions and declined readings. The refusal text tells the reader to cover the bullet in a criterion or ask the split as a question, so one correction round repairs it. The doc states the heuristic's limits. The declared share (10%, an estimate) lets the replay pass this rule.

risks.risk: False acceptance: a dropped bullet whose words are common in other criteria is judged covered.
risks.mitigation: Accepted by design (the target is the wholesale drop that caused the 2026-10-29 rejection); the corpus case built from the verbatim request of this job shows the real shape is caught, and the limit is written in the doc comment.

risks.risk: The reader is not told of the rule, so the first reading of an affected job can be refused (reader prompt set has 2 tokens of headroom; prompts are out of scope).
risks.mitigation: The refusal reaches the reader as its one correction (reading.rs:740-761) and names the missing bullet and the question route, which is enough to repair the reading.

risks.risk: The verbatim request in the first corpus case could be refused first by another check (for example check_defined_terms or check_outcome_state) because of its wording, hiding the new check.
risks.mitigation: The new step is last, so an earlier refusal would show in `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` as 'refused by <other check>'. The request text uses no ladder/tier/layer/rung word, no delivery verb, no governance path and no job id (read from the brief). If one still refuses, step 4 rebuilds the case from the same two bullets and says so in its `source` string, keeping the omitted-bullet and split-words shape.

risks.risk: The id of the rejected 2026-10-29 job is not in any file the planner can read (HISTORY.txt and the repository hold no record of it), so the doc cannot cite it by id.
risks.mitigation: The doc names the date and the request of job 20261029-111121-fzx0 that describes it, which is what the criterion asks ('names the 2026-10-29 job'); the doc test asserts the date string, not an id.

demonstrations.method: `coverage_cases()` in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs, added to `cases()`. Each case starts from `case(..)`/`base_reading(request)` (whose criteria are the request's bullets verbatim) and removes or edits one field. Case ids (all new; each pins `bullets_expected`): `request-coverage-omitted-bullet-in-job-fzx0-request` (the verbatim request of this job, second bullet removed from the criteria; Refuse `check_request_coverage`; tags dash-bullet, acceptance-bullet-omitted, request-mentions-split-without-allowing); `request-coverage-all-bullets-covered-in-job-fzx0-request` (Accept); `request-coverage-numbered-parts-one-omitted` (`1.`/`2.`/`3.` under the heading, part 2 dropped; Refuse; number-dot-parts); `request-coverage-star-bullets-covered-by-one-merged-criterion` (Accept; acceptance-bullet-covered-across-criteria; star-bullet); `request-coverage-request-allows-split` (Accept; request-allows-split); `request-coverage-request-forbids-split` ('Do not split this job.', Refuse; request-mentions-split-without-allowing); `request-coverage-reading-asks-the-split-as-a-question` (reading.question set, bullet omitted; Accept; split-proposed-as-question); `request-coverage-no-heading-not-read-today` (bullets without heading, one omitted; Accept; no-acceptance-heading; a pinned known gap like the existing `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today`); `request-coverage-paren-parts-under-heading-not-read-today` (`1)` parts, 0 bullets; Accept; number-paren-parts); `request-coverage-bullet-after-the-section-is-not-acceptance` (a bullet after a blank line following the section, left uncovered; Accept; bullet-after-acceptance-section). Existing cases that already prove the accept side with a heading: `steward-three-dash-bullets` (refusal_corpus.rs:1677) and `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying` (:1751); `numbered-paren-parts-not-read-today` and `lettered-paren-parts-not-read-today` (:1719, :1732) cover the `N)` and `(a)` forms without a heading. Forms with no bearing on this rule (a cited job, a retry complaint, a governance or crate-relative path, a brand word, an environment variable) are read as ordinary words only inside bullets; `follow-up-on-a-job-the-reading-ignores` (:1764) keeps its refusal by `check_prior_result_and_scope`, which runs first.
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` gets the stated outcome for every case, `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` finds `check_request_coverage` among the checks that refuse, `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` finds the 7 new tags held, and `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` agrees on the error text.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step, `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` cannot see the check; with the step but no case it fails by naming `check_request_coverage`; with the check removed the omitted-bullet cases get 'accepted' instead of Refuse.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` via `run(c)` in refusal_corpus.rs:2595 (exists). Fixtures: `case(..)` and `base_reading(..)` (refusal_corpus.rs:230, 161, exist). `reading_source()` (refusal_corpus.rs:2670) gains `include_str!("../src/reading/coverage.rs")` (step 4). No double; the result of the check is never stubbed.

demonstrations.method: A test `request_coverage_has_one_step_line` in reading.rs, modelled on `environment_reach_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs:5376): it takes the body of `refusing_check` from `reading_source()`, asserts exactly one line equals `step!(check_request_coverage(reading, request));`, that it comes right after `step!(check_reading_references(reading, repo_files));`, and that the text before `pub fn check_reading_acceptance(` contains "[`check_request_coverage`]". The existing corpus test that scans check_reading_acceptance for a direct check call (refusal_corpus.rs ~2969) still passes, and the existing adjacency tests are unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: One step line, last, and the doc link; Grep `step!(check_request_coverage` over crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs gives one line.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check were a direct call or the doc link missing, the equality or `contains` assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Source text via `reading_source()` (reading.rs:1491, exists; step 2 adds coverage.rs to its list). No double.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks on the whole workspace. The producer fixes any fixture that the new check newly refuses (see step 6 and the risk on fixtures).
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0; the full test run includes the other crates that reach `check_reading_acceptance` (cli drain tests, steward, run tests, hestia).
demonstrations.fails_without: Any formatting difference, warning or failing test makes the command exit non-zero.
demonstrations.seam: The cargo commands themselves; no fixture is added for this criterion.

demonstrations.method: Test `request_coverage_refusal_is_declared_intended` in reading.rs. It (1) calls `replay_declaration` with a behavior criterion 'The change refuses more readings: expected 10% of newly refused readings' and asserts `share == Some(10)`, and (2) shows the refusal rate rises: a reading that every earlier step accepts (`refusing_check` on the same reading and a request with no `Acceptance:` heading gives None) is refused by `check_request_coverage` once the request carries a heading and a bullet the reading omits.
demonstrations.observes: The declared share parses as 10; the same reading flips from accepted to refused by the new check alone.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the second half returns None and the `assert_eq!(name, "check_request_coverage")` fails; without the declared sentence the share is None.
demonstrations.seam: `replay_declaration` (exists, used at refusal_corpus.rs:2773) and `refusing_check` with `governed_reading` (exists). No double. The 10% is an estimate, not a measurement; it is labelled so in the doc and the changelog.

demonstrations.method: Add one item to `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` in CHANGELOG.md that contains `reading::check_request_coverage`, 'refuses more readings', 'higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' (the text may wrap; tests collapse white space). Test `request_coverage_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause` (reading.rs, modelled on `scope_limit_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause`, reading.rs:8493) parses the Unreleased items and asserts the item holds those phrases.
demonstrations.observes: The Unreleased item for the check exists and carries the four phrases.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing or reworded item fails the `contains` assertions.
demonstrations.seam: `include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md")` in the test, as the sibling tests do (exists). No double.

demonstrations.method: The same test as criterion 7 also collapses the `///` lines above `pub fn check_request_coverage(` from `reading_source()` and asserts they hold '2026-10-29', 'rejected for a split the reading chose', 'only as a question, never by dropping a bullet', 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'estimate'.
demonstrations.observes: The doc comment of the new check names the 2026-10-29 job and states the question-only rule.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the doc lacks a phrase, or coverage.rs is not in `reading_source()`, the test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Source text via `reading_source()`, which step 2 extends with coverage.rs. No double.
